dedupe_keys.name: fema building code adoption tracking bcat

description: FEMA's Building Code Adoption Tracking (BCAT) follows building code adoption by state, local, tribal and territorial governments and rates whether communities have adopted current or recent editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code without weakening their natural hazard provisions. It reports resistance for damaging wind, hurricane wind, tornado, flood and seismic hazards and for combined hazards; in the third quarter of 2026 it reported 167.3 million people, 50% of the population, living in jurisdictions with hazard-resistant codes, with shares by hazard ranging from 22% for tornado to 63% for hurricane wind. FEMA updates BCAT data quarterly in an ArcGIS portal, with regional fact sheets updated annually; the page was last updated on 7 July 2026. Coverage: U.S. jurisdictions. Access: interactive portal and fact sheets. Licence: U.S. government information; free. Caveats: the page read here does not name its underlying data source, and adoption does not measure enforcement. Simulation uses are code-year and code-strength assumptions for building fragility and community resilience models. Related records: ICC Digital Codes.
